title: CE comparison morphism and bottom-interval quasi-isomorphisms
statement: With the hypotheses of the CE decalage comparison, there is a family of spectral-object morphisms from the decalage model to the Grothendieck spectral object, natural for all presentation comparisons and all filtered lifts of the prescribed total map. Only the components on intervals from minus infinity to an arbitrary cutoff are asserted invertible. No invertibility on general intervals is asserted.

proof.text: Use the natural extended-tower left exactness comparison to move G through the smart horizontal cuts. Then use the inclusion-normalized total-truncation/decalage tower isomorphism, including both endpoints. Apply the mapping-cone cohomology spectral-object functor. This gives the source comparison s, natural for every prescribed filtered lift.
Apply the resolved CE smart-cut comparison c to Q(F(P.J)). It constructs the interval spectral-object morphism and proves the bottom components invertible, naturally for presentation comparisons.

Compute RF(P.X) using the specified injective resolution P.J. Apply the canonical truncation, RG and homology spectral-object functors to this natural derived isomorphism, obtaining r from the Grothendieck spectral object to the intermediate object Q(F(P.J)).

The required morphism is s inverse, followed by c, followed by r inverse. Evaluation at each bottom interval is a composite of isomorphisms. Naturality is obtained by conjugating the proved source tower square and the specified-resolution square, then composing with the naturality equation for c. No choice of comparison data is used to define an object.
